manifest.name: Payment Provider: Mollie
manifest.summary: A Dutch payment provider covering several European countries.
manifest.author: Odoo S.A., Applix BV, Droggol Infotech Pvt. Ltd.

models._description: Payment Provider (Mollie credential: single API key, Test or Live)
Payment Transaction (Mollie Payments API redirect flow; no new fields, 5 override methods)
relations: no new fields; 5 methods overriding payment's rendering/notification hooks (_get_specific_rendering_values, _mollie_prepare_payment_request_payload, _extract_reference, _extract_amount_data, _apply_updates)

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on the base.group_system field group guarding mollie_api_key (the sole credential).

views.note: xml_loc=39 across three data files: payment_provider_views.xml inherits payment.payment_provider_form to add the Mollie API Key field (password, invisible unless code=='mollie'); payment_mollie_templates.xml defines the QWeb redirect_form (a method='get' auto-submit form to the Mollie-hosted checkout url with url_params re-attached); payment_provider_data.xml seeds payment.provider_mollie and wires redirect_form_view_id. No own model views.

behavioral_notes.observation: For a Mollie transaction, _get_specific_rendering_values builds a payload via _mollie_prepare_payment_request_payload (description=tx.reference; amount={currency, value formatted to CURRENCY_MINOR_UNITS decimals}; locale clamped to const.SUPPORTED_LOCALES else 'en_US'; method=[const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING.get(payment_method_code) -- e.g. card->creditcard, apple_pay->applepay, bank_transfer->banktransfer, kbc_cbc->kbc, p24->przelewy24, sepa_direct_debit->directdebit]; redirectUrl=<return_url>?ref=<reference>; webhookUrl=<webhook_url>?ref=<reference>) and POSTs it to '/payments' via the parent engine's _send_api_request. It stores provider_reference = payment_data['id'] up-front (so the status can be re-fetched after redirection), then reads the Mollie-hosted checkout link payment_data['_links']['checkout']['href'], splits its query string out into url_params, and hands {api_url, url_params} to the QWeb redirect_form so the browser is auto-submitted to Mollie's hosted checkout page. On ValidationError the tx is _set_error and an empty dict is returned. The ?ref= is carried because Mollie does not echo the transaction reference back on redirect. None of this server-to-server HTTP nor the hosted-redirect handoff is visible in Python field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: MollieController.mollie_webhook (/payment/mollie/webhook) + mollie_return_from_checkout (/payment/mollie/return) -> _verify_and_process re-fetches the payment by id from Mollie (GET /payments/<provider_reference>)
behavioral_notes.observation: Both the public csrf=False POST webhook and the public GET/POST redirect-return route call the SAME staticmethod _verify_and_process(data). Mollie posts only an opaque payment id; the Odoo reference travels in the URL query as ?ref=, so _search_by_reference('mollie', data) routes through _extract_reference -> data['ref'] to find the tx. Crucially, the inbound POST body is NOT trusted for state: _verify_and_process re-fetches the authoritative payment object via tx_sudo._send_api_request('GET', f'/payments/{tx_sudo.provider_reference}') (Bearer-authenticated, server-to-server) and only THEN calls tx_sudo._process('mollie', verified_data). Authenticity therefore comes from the trusted Mollie-side re-fetch over the API key, not from a signature on the notification. On a fetch ValidationError it logs an error and processes nothing; the webhook returns '' and the return route redirects to /payment/status. This re-fetch-by-id trust model is invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates -> Mollie payment status -> payment state machine; method back-mapping via cardLabel
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates reads the re-fetched payment object. It refines the payment.method: when method=='creditcard' it drills into details.cardLabel (lowercased -- e.g. 'visa','mastercard') and resolves a payment.method via _get_from_code(..., mapping=const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING). It then maps Mollie's status to payment's guarded state machine: 'pending'/'open' -> _set_pending; 'authorized' -> _set_authorized; 'paid' -> _set_done; 'expired'/'canceled'/'failed' -> _set_canceled (with the status in the message); anything else logs and _set_error. _extract_amount_data pulls amount.value/amount.currency from the same object for the amount check. The status->state mapping and the cardLabel brand back-resolution are invisible to metadata.

payment_mollie ships NO 'requests' import; outbound HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine, configured by three overrides: _build_request_url joins endpoints onto 'https://api.mollie.com/v2/' (urls.urljoin, endpoint.strip('/')); _build_request_headers returns Accept/Content-Type application/json, 'Authorization: Bearer <mollie_api_key>', and a Mollie partner User-Agent 'Odoo/<server_version> MollieNativeOdoo/<module_version>' (per Mollie's user-agent-strings integration requirement); _parse_response_error pulls response.json()['detail']. Auth is thus a single Bearer API key (Test or Live, chosen by the merchant), with no separate webhook secret -- consistent with the re-fetch-by-id verification model. This Bearer scheme and the api.mollie.com base are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, key, no SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; endpoints https://api.mollie.com/v2/ (the live REST base reached via _build_request_url; concrete endpoints POST /payments and GET /payments/<id>) and https://www.mollie.com (manifest website only). Auth is HTTP Bearer with mollie_api_key. There is no python Mollie SDK and no client-side JS SDK: card data is entered on Mollie's own hosted checkout page after redirect (the module ships no static/src assets, only description icons), so PCI scope stays with Mollie. The whole acquirer link -- outbound create-payment + the inbound webhook/return re-fetch -- is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of it is reachable from model/field metadata; it was established only by reading payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py.

extract_frontend.py reports present=false: 0 JS files, 0 XML templates beyond the server-rendered QWeb redirect_form, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, no asset bundles. Unlike Stripe/Xendit there is no client-side SDK and no PaymentForm patch: the module relies entirely on the generic 'payment' redirect-with-form-submission flow, and the only template is the server-side auto-submit redirect_form that POSTs/GETs the browser to Mollie's hosted checkout. So gap #3 is effectively empty here -- the browser-side acquirer interaction happens on Mollie's hosted page, not in Odoo-shipped JS.

it_architecture.application: payment_mollie (Mollie acquirer adapter for the payment engine; _inherit-only, no own models/views)
software_services: /payment/mollie/return (redirect-return: http GET/POST, csrf=False, save_session=False; re-fetches the payment by id then redirects to /payment/status)
/payment/mollie/webhook (async notification: http POST, csrf=False; re-fetches the payment by id then _process)
data_objects: payment.transaction (Mollie Payments API redirect flow; no new fields)
logical_data_erm: payment.transaction -> payment.provider (provider_id; provider_code=='mollie' gates every override)
external: payment.transaction reference carried as the ?ref= URL parameter (cross-system lookup key via _extract_reference -> data['ref'])
external: payment.transaction.provider_reference == Mollie payment id (payment_data['id']; used to re-fetch GET /payments/<id>)
information_flows: depends: payment (inherits the provider/transaction engine + _send_api_request request plumbing)
outbound (create): _get_specific_rendering_values -> POST https://api.mollie.com/v2/payments (Bearer mollie_api_key) -> Mollie-hosted checkout url
browser: server-rendered redirect_form auto-submits (GET) to the Mollie-hosted checkout page; card details entered on Mollie's page (no Odoo-shipped JS/SDK)
inbound (webhook): Mollie -> /payment/mollie/webhook?ref=... -> _verify_and_process -> GET /payments/<id> re-fetch -> _process -> payment state machine
frontend_components: redirect_form (server-side QWeb auto-submit GET form to the Mollie-hosted checkout url; no client-side JS/OWL)

external_integrations.sdk: none (no python Mollie SDK; no client-side JS SDK -- card entry on Mollie's hosted checkout); HTTP via payment.provider._send_api_request
endpoints: https://api.mollie.com/v2/ (POST /payments to create the hosted payment; GET /payments/<id> to re-fetch authoritative status)
external_integrations.auth: HTTP Bearer -- 'Authorization: Bearer <mollie_api_key>' (single Test-or-Live key; no separate webhook secret) (_build_request_headers)
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration. Outbound server-to-server REST to api.mollie.com/v2 (POST /payments) authenticated with a single Bearer API key creates a Mollie-hosted checkout to which the browser is redirected; inbound settlement arrives as a notification (webhook) or a redirect-return, but neither is trusted on its body -- the server re-fetches GET /payments/<id> by the stored provider_reference and processes THAT. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Mollie endpoints, the Bearer-key auth, or the re-fetch-by-id verification model are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py. Distinctive vs signature-based acquirers: Mollie webhooks/returns carry only an id, so authenticity is delegated to a Bearer-authenticated re-fetch rather than an HMAC/checksum on the notification.

capabilities: Accept European card / local-method payments via Mollie hosted checkout (redirect flow: card, Apple Pay, Bancontact/KBC-CBC, iDEAL, Przelewy24, SEPA direct debit, bank transfer, etc.)
Asynchronous settlement confirmation via a Mollie webhook plus a redirect-return route (both re-fetching the payment by id)
Multi-currency acceptance across the Mollie-supported set (EUR, GBP, USD, and ~30 currencies in const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES)
value_streams: Collect-Payment (redirect): _get_specific_rendering_values -> POST /payments (api.mollie.com) -> browser redirect to Mollie-hosted checkout -> /payment/mollie/return -> re-fetch GET /payments/<id> -> _process -> /payment/status
Confirm-Settlement (async): Mollie -> /payment/mollie/webhook -> re-fetch GET /payments/<id> -> _apply_updates status mapping -> _set_pending/_set_authorized/_set_done/_set_canceled
Settle: Mollie status 'paid' -> _set_done -> downstream post-process settlement (account_payment / sale)
information_concepts: payment.provider (Mollie credential: a single Test-or-Live API key)
payment.transaction (mapped to a Mollie payment; keyed by ?ref= reference and provider_reference=payment id)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; mollie_api_key is restricted to base.group_system; everything else inherits payment's groups/record rules)
policies: Notification trust by re-fetch: neither the webhook nor the redirect-return body is trusted for state; _verify_and_process re-fetches GET /payments/<provider_reference> over the Bearer API key and processes that authoritative object (no notification signature/secret)
Supported currencies bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES; others filtered out by _get_supported_currencies
Checkout locale bounded to const.SUPPORTED_LOCALES (fallback en_US)
Amount formatted to CURRENCY_MINOR_UNITS decimals for the Mollie amount.value
Single API key gated by the base.group_system field group; chosen Test vs Live by the merchant
stakeholders: Merchant / Company (res.company, holds the Mollie account & API key)
Mollie (external acquirer / PSP for the Netherlands and several European countries)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_mollie is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the payer (cardholder / bank-method user) and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Mollie's European card / local-payment-method network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (a single Mollie API key + currency/locale/payment-method enablement), service provisioning (creating a Mollie hosted payment and confirming its status per transaction), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.mollie.com link plus the webhook/return re-fetch settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Mollie realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe / payment_xendit metamodels (network/support) and the parent payment engine.

standard_capabilities: hosted-redirect acceptance of European card and local methods via the Mollie Payments API v2 (POST /payments; form-submission redirect flow)
asynchronous settlement via a webhook plus a redirect-return route, both re-fetching the authoritative payment by id (no signature needed)
multi-currency acceptance across const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (~30 currencies; amount in CURRENCY_MINOR_UNITS decimals)
automatic provider setup/teardown via post_init_hook setup_provider / uninstall_hook reset_payment_provider
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting payments in the Netherlands and wider Europe via Mollie (iDEAL, Bancontact, cards, SEPA, etc.)
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
multi-currency European e-commerce where card data should stay on the PSP's hosted page (PCI scope offloaded to Mollie)
common_gaps: no tokenization / saved cards (README 'Not implemented'; no payment.token vaulting, no off-session/recurring charge path)

no manual capture / authorize-then-capture and no void operation (README 'Manual capture' not implemented; charge is immediate -- though _apply_updates can record an 'authorized' status if Mollie returns one)
no in-module refund operation (README 'Refunds' not implemented; no _send_refund_request override -- refunds done via the Mollie dashboard or a downstream module)
no merchant self-onboarding -- the API key is entered manually on the provider form (no Connect-style flow)

the public-URL/HTTPS requirement for the webhook means local/dev instances need a tunnel; with no webhook secret, authenticity rests entirely on the Bearer-authenticated re-fetch and a correct provider_reference
currency/locale support bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES / const.SUPPORTED_LOCALES; others are filtered/fallback-ed
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here
drive_hints: odoo shell: print([m for m in dir(env['payment.transaction']) if '_mollie' in m])

curl 'https://<host>/payment/mollie/webhook' -d 'ref=<unknown-ref>' (csrf=False, auth=public) -> _search_by_reference finds nothing -> no processing (the server would otherwise re-fetch GET /payments/<id> from Mollie before trusting any state)
Mollie testing: https://docs.mollie.com/overview/testing -- test card 4111111111111111, expiry 123, CVC 123 (README; HTTPS required)

open_questions: Exact Mollie Payments API v2 request/response payloads beyond the fields built in _mollie_prepare_payment_request_payload and consumed in _apply_updates (e.g. the full details/cardLabel object).
Real-world distribution of Mollie transaction states and method mix (card vs iDEAL/Bancontact/SEPA), and how often the 'authorized' interim state occurs (no runtime row counts captured).
How refunds/chargebacks are handled operationally given no in-module refund override (likely via the Mollie dashboard or a downstream module).
Whether instances reliably register the webhook (public HTTPS URL reachable) vs rely on the redirect-return route, given both ultimately re-fetch the same payment by id.
